# Transformer Attention

## The Intuition

Before transformers, sequence modeling (RNNs, LSTMs) processed tokens one at a time, carrying a fixed-size hidden state forward. This made it hard to relate distant tokens and to parallelize.

**Attention** solves this: instead of compressing everything into a single vector, every token can *look at every other token* in the sequence and decide how much information to pull from each. The result is a context-aware representation for every position simultaneously.

## The Three Matrices

For a sequence of tokens, the model projects the input embeddings into three roles:

| Matrix | Role | Analogy |
|--------|------|---------|
| **Q** (Queries) | "What am I looking for?" | A search query |
| **K** (Keys) | "What do I contain?" | An index entry |
| **V** (Values) | "What information do I actually hold?" | The document body |

## The Formula

$$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V$$

1. **Score** – `QKᵀ` gives a matrix where entry *(i, j)* is the dot-product between query *i* and key *j*. High values mean "token *i* should attend to token *j*."
